name: SRTM (Shuttle Radar Topography Mission), C-band, v3/SRTMGL1
resolution: 30 m (1 arc-second) posting; native radar swath resolution ~30 m; C-band, Feb 2000 vintage
license: Public domain (NASA/USGS); no attribution legally required, but courtesy credit customary
download_route: Already the project's DEM, via Mapzen/Tilezen 'Terrarium' PNG tiles on the AWS Open Data 'elevation-tiles-prod' bucket: https://s3.amazonaws.com/elevation-tiles-prod/terrarium/{z}/{x}/{y}.png (verified HTTP 200 for z14 tile over the site). No AWS account, no key. Also raw .hgt via USGS EarthExplorer (needs free login) or opentopography.org.
notes: Current baseline in scripts/build-terrain.js. C-band radar has known vegetation-canopy and coastal/water-edge noise; LE90 ~8.5 m, RMSE ~5.4 m per published DEM intercomparisons. This is the source the project's README explicitly flags as turning the 25 m coastal ridge into a mountain when over-exaggerated.

name: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (ESA/Airbus, from TanDEM-X)
resolution: 30 m (1 arc-second) posting over India (GLO-30 uses ~1 arcsec spacing up to |lat|<50 deg); tile is a 1 deg x 1 deg Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF
license: Copernicus DEM licence (free, worldwide, commercial+non-commercial use; attribution required: 'Copernicus DEM ... accessed on DATE from registry.opendata.aws/copernicus-dem')
download_route: Anonymous AWS S3, verified: `curl -I https://copernicus-dem-30m.s3.amazonaws.com/Copernicus_DSM_COG_10_N12_00_E080_00_DEM/Copernicus_DSM_COG_10_N12_00_E080_00_DEM.tif` returns HTTP 200 (tile covering 12-13N, 80-81E, which contains the whole 4 km build-terrain.js square). Also `aws s3 cp --no-sign-request`, or bulk via OpenTopography's Global DEM API (portal.opentopography.org, key-free for GLO-30 bulk S3 access at s3://raster/COP30/, though their web API historically wants a free API key for the convenience endpoint).
notes: THE RECOMMENDED UPGRADE. Same 30 m nominal posting as the current SRTM source, but from 2011-2015 TanDEM-X bistatic X-band InSAR (not 2000 C-band), edited and void-filled by DLR/Airbus. Published accuracy is measurably better: LE90 ~7.7 m vs SRTM's ~8.5 m, RMSE ~4.9 m vs ~5.4 m, and independent studies report Copernicus DEM as the most accurate freely available global DEM, roughly halving SRTM's stated absolute vertical error (~4 m vs ~9 m in some comparisons). It will not add texture the current DEM lacks (still ~30 m posting, still no plinths) but it removes real C-band noise and vegetation bias along exactly the low-relief coastal terrain (the granite ridge, the beach edge) that the project's README says the current DEM already mis-renders. Format: single-band float32 Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF, ~3600x3600 px per 1x1 deg tile. Decoding it needs a (small) GeoTIFF/COG reader rather than the current hand-rolled PNG decoder in build-terrain.js -- non-trivial but bounded work, no new dependency required if written by hand similarly.

name: Copernicus DEM GLO-90
resolution: 90 m (3 arc-second) posting, worldwide
license: Same Copernicus DEM licence as GLO-30 (free, attribution required)
download_route: s3://copernicus-dem-90m (anonymous, no-sign-request), Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF, tile naming Copernicus_DSM_COG_30_N12_00_E080_00_DEM
notes: Coarser than what the project already uses; only relevant as a smaller/faster fallback, not an upgrade.

name: ALOS World 3D - 30m (AW3D30), JAXA
resolution: ~30 m (approx. 1 arc-second) horizontal posting, from 2006-2011 PRISM stereo optical imagery
license: Free for commercial and non-commercial use under JAXA's AW3D30 Terms of Use
download_route: REQUIRES ACCOUNT REGISTRATION: register at https://www.eorc.jaxa.jp/ALOS/en/aw3d30/registration.htm, verify email, log into https://www.eorc.jaxa.jp/ALOS/en/aw3d30/data/index.htm, then click the 1x1 or 5x5 deg tile on the map to download a GeoTIFF zip.
notes: Optical stereo-derived, so it does not carry SRTM/TanDEM-X's radar penetration issues, but registration is a hard blocker for this project's stated key-free/no-registration constraint.

name: NASADEM (SRTM void-filled + ICESat/ASTER blended, NASA)
resolution: 30 m (1 arc-second) posting
license: Public domain / open, per NASA EOSDIS Data Use and Citation Guidance
download_route: REQUIRES a free NASA Earthdata Login account. Distributed via LP DAAC / Earthdata Search, tile naming e.g. n12e080.hgt / .tif. No anonymous AWS bucket for NASADEM was found (registry.opendata.aws/nasadem returns 404 as of this check).
notes: Reprocesses the same 2000 SRTM radar pass with better void-filling and control from ICESat/ASTER/GDEM3 -- a real quality bump over raw SRTM, comparable in spirit to Copernicus DEM but the download path requires registration, unlike Copernicus DEM's anonymous S3 bucket. Prefer Copernicus DEM GLO-30 for a key-free project.

name: ASTER GDEM v3 (ASTGTM v003), NASA/METI
resolution: 30 m (1 arc-second) posting, from 2000-2013 ASTER optical stereo
license: Open, per EOSDIS Data Use and Citation Guidance; DOI citation requested (10.5067/ASTER/ASTGTM.003)
download_route: REQUIRES free NASA Earthdata Login; download via LP DAAC / Earthdata Search as COG or NetCDF4.
notes: Generally noisier than SRTM/Copernicus DEM in published comparisons (more artifacts). Registration requirement rules it out for this project regardless.

name: CartoDEM (Cartosat-1 stereo DEM), ISRO/NRSC Bhuvan
resolution: 30 m (1 arc-second) posting is the freely downloadable tier; a 10 m posting product exists but is priced/restricted, and anything finer than 10 m needs High Resolution Image Clearance Committee approval
license: NRSC open-data policy for the 30 m tier ('free download'); finer products are priced or require government/committee clearance
download_route: Bhuvan portal (bhuvan.nrsc.gov.in) / Bhuvan Open Data Archive. Requires a Bhuvan user login even for the free 30 m tier, and the FAQ documents a 20-tiles-per-day download cap. No sub-30 m data is obtainable without ISRO clearance.
notes: India's own national DEM is not a resolution upgrade over SRTM/Copernicus at the freely downloadable tier (still 30 m), and it requires account registration, so it fails this project's key-free constraint even before considering resolution.

name: Open LiDAR / drone survey of Mahabalipuram monuments
resolution: n/a - not found as a public downloadable dataset
license: n/a
download_route: None found. ASI is reported (2025 press coverage, e.g. organiser.org) to use LiDAR/drone/photogrammetry generally for monument documentation, and its Underwater Archaeology Wing resumed offshore survey work at Mahabalipuram in 2025, but no open, downloadable point cloud, DTM, or orthomosaic for this specific site was located on any ASI, NRSC/Bhuvan, or academic repository.
notes: Searched ASI's own site, general LiDAR-in-archaeology coverage, and academic/photogrammetry sources. Nothing citable and downloadable turned up for this specific site -- this is a real gap, not a research shortcoming: report it as 'none found', not 'none exists', since ASI survey outputs are often not published as open data even when the survey itself happened.

name: Mapzen/Tilezen Terrarium tiles (AWS Terrain Tiles) -- current project source
resolution: PNG-encoded, 256x256 px tiles; at z14 pixel spacing is ~9-10 m but the underlying value for most of India is oversampled/interpolated SRTM at native 30 m -- no real added detail past z12
license: Blend of sources per-region; for India, SRTM (public domain). Attribution: 'Mapzen / AWS Terrain Tiles (SRTM et al.)', already how build-terrain.js credits it.
download_route: s3://elevation-tiles-prod/terrarium/{z}/{x}/{y}.png, anonymous, verified reachable. This is exactly what scripts/build-terrain.js already fetches.
notes: This is a delivery mechanism for SRTM (see dem-srtm), not a distinct elevation source for India. Switching the URL pattern in build-terrain.js from this to the Copernicus DEM GeoTIFF tile is the concrete upgrade path.

name: Mapbox Terrain-RGB
resolution: Varies by zoom, blends SRTM/ArcticDEM/etc; comparable underlying source resolution to Terrarium for India
license: Mapbox proprietary tileset terms
download_route: Requires a Mapbox access token / API key for every tile request.
notes: Not fetched/verified live (would require an account to test). Ruled out on the stated need for key-free access regardless of resolution.

name: MapTiler terrain / elevation tiles
resolution: Similar blended global sources
license: MapTiler proprietary/API terms
download_route: Requires a MapTiler API key.
notes: Not fetched. Ruled out for the same key requirement as Mapbox.

name: Sentinel-2 L2A (ESA Copernicus)
resolution: 10 m for visible/NIR bands (B02/B03/B04/B08); 20 m and 60 m for other bands
license: Free, full and open per Copernicus data policy; attribution 'Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data'
download_route: Anonymous S3: s3://sentinel-s2-l2a (no-sign-request); scene discovery via the Element 84 Earth Search STAC API (earth-search.aws.element84.com) which needs no key for search or asset download.
notes: Good ground-texture source for a coastal basemap at true 10 m; cloud-free scene selection over Mahabalipuram needs a STAC search by date/cloud-cover, not fetched here but the endpoint itself needs no key.

name: ESA WorldCover 10 m (2020/2021)
resolution: 10 m land-cover classification, derived from Sentinel-1 + Sentinel-2
license: CC BY 4.0, attribution required
download_route: Anonymous S3: `aws s3 sync s3://esa-worldcover/v200/2021/map /local/path --no-sign-request`. Viewer/Terrascope access needs login; the S3 bucket does not.
notes: Useful as a land-cover mask (vegetation vs bare rock vs built-up) to drive material/texture choices, not as photographic texture itself.

name: Bhuvan (ISRO/NRSC) satellite imagery
resolution: Varies by product (LISS-III ~24 m to Cartosat ~2.5 m for some layers); not itemised on the fetched page
license: Bhuvan geoportal terms grant a 'non-exclusive, non-transferable licence to access' -- not a clean open licence
download_route: Bhuvan Open Data Archive / Bhoonidhi VISTA, generally requires portal login for download.
notes: Ruled out for a key-free static site; Sentinel-2 already covers the 10 m tier with a cleaner licence and no login.

name: OpenAerialMap
resolution: Varies per contributed image (community drone/aerial uploads, often sub-metre where available)
license: Openly licensed per-image (project describes itself as a commons of openly licensed imagery); exact licence is per-contribution
download_route: Browse via the OAM browser / API; no coverage confirmation for Mahabalipuram was found on the fetched page and no search was completed against the OAM catalog for this specific site.
notes: Coverage for this exact site is UNVERIFIED -- the page itself gave no site-specific information and the OAM catalog was not queried directly. Worth checking oam.hotosm.org's search API directly in a follow-up.

name: GEBCO_2024 Grid
resolution: 15 arc-second global grid (~460 m at the equator)
license: Public domain; attribution requested ('acknowledge the source'); explicitly NOT for navigation/safety-at-sea use
download_route: download.gebco.net -- the GEBCO Grid Subsetting App lets you draw/enter a bounding box and export netCDF, GeoTIFF or Esri ASCII without login.
notes: Coarse (460 m) relative to the project's onshore terrain grid (~21 m), but this is standard for global bathymetry and is exactly what a Bay-of-Bengal 'sea' base in the scene needs -- shelf-scale shape, not nearshore detail. The project already clamps its own DEM's seafloor to -6 m for scale reasons, so GEBCO would mainly matter if the scene ever extends the sea plane further offshore.

name: OSM natural=coastline (already used by the project)
resolution: Vector line, mapped detail (project's fetch pulled a 299-node way for this stretch)
license: ODbL, attribution required
download_route: Already fetched into data/mamallapuram-coastline.geojson via Overpass; file's own _note documents it as OSM natural=coastline, fetched 2026-09-06, credited '© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL'.
notes: No changes needed here; listed for completeness since section C asked about coastline data specifically.

name: NIO / ASI Underwater Archaeology Wing offshore survey findings
resolution: n/a -- point/feature-level archaeological findings, not a gridded dataset
license: n/a -- no open dataset located
download_route: None. Findings (a submerged wall, steps, chiselled blocks ~800 m offshore at ~27 ft/8 m depth, reported by NIO divers after the Dec 2004 tsunami withdrawal, plus an earlier 2002 SES/NIO expedition) are documented in press coverage and papers (e.g. a ResearchGate PDF 'Underwater investigations off Mahabalipuram, Tamil Nadu, India'), not as downloadable geospatial data.
notes: Real and citable as narrative/history content (already adjacent to the kind of provenance this project cares about), but not usable as a data layer -- there is no published point cloud, bathymetric survey grid, or GIS file from NIO's surveys that could be dropped into the scene.

name: Tamil Nadu / Mahabalipuram historic shoreline-change studies
resolution: n/a -- academic DSAS (Digital Shoreline Analysis System) transect studies, not a single reusable dataset
license: n/a -- journal articles, not open data
download_route: None as reusable GIS data. Multiple published studies exist (a ScienceDirect paper on 8th-century coastal uplift and the Shore Temple; a DSAS-based Mahabalipuram-to-Odiyur-Lake study reporting up to 7.5 m/yr erosion and up to 119 m retreat in nearby stretches over 17 years; other Tamil Nadu coast erosion papers), but none publish an open shapefile/geojson of historic shorelines for direct reuse.
notes: Confirms the coast has measurably moved (erosion-dominated near Mahabalipuram per the cited papers) but there is no ready-to-use dataset -- only citable findings for the site's written content, not for the geometry pipeline.

name: OSM completeness audit, bbox (12.60,80.17)-(12.64,80.21)
resolution: n/a -- live Overpass query executed 2026-09-07
license: ODbL
download_route: POST to https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter with a QL query for building/historic/tourism/natural=rock|bare_rock in the given bbox; query executed successfully (HTTP 200, 337 elements returned).
notes: Real measured counts: 337 elements total (114 nodes, 215 ways, 8 relations). 205 features tagged building=*, of which exactly 1 carries a height tag and 0 carry building:levels (matches the README's claim for its smaller CORE bbox almost exactly). 28 historic=* features (14 as nodes -- caves/mandapams/Arjuna's Penance etc. mapped as points only; 14 as ways/relations -- the five rathas, Shore Temple, Pancha Rathas grouping, etc. mapped as real outlines). 125 tourism=* features (museum, information, hotel, attraction, guest_house, viewpoint). 11 natural=bare_rock/rock features, all mapped as ways (none as nodes) -- the granite outcrops are already outlined, not just pinned.

name: Google Open Buildings
resolution: Building-footprint polygons with a 0.65-1.0 confidence score; presence/geometry only
license: User's choice of CC BY 4.0 or ODbL 1.0
download_route: India is covered (145+ countries incl. India). Download via interactive map, a Colab notebook, HDX, gsutil (full 178 GB set), or Google Earth Engine asset -- none need an API key for the open download routes.
notes: NO HEIGHT DATA -- footprints only, explicitly 'no information ... other than its geometry'. Would only help fill footprint gaps, never heights, and OSM's own footprint coverage in the audited bbox (205 buildings) is likely already denser/more curated for this specific tourist core than a global ML-detected set.

name: Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints
resolution: ML-detected building polygons; global dataset notes 110M of its footprint edits are primarily contributed in India
license: CDLA Permissive 2.0
download_route: dataset-links.csv (hosted on Azure Blob Storage) indexes tiles by Bing quadkey; no bounding-box or country-level simple download -- requires identifying the right quadkey tile(s) for Mahabalipuram and downloading the matching line-delimited GeoJSON (.csv.gz).
notes: DOES include height attributes for India per the fetched page (worth independently verifying per-building once a tile is pulled, since ML-derived heights carry their own uncertainty). No API key needed but the quadkey-based access is more involved than a direct bbox query.

name: Overture Maps Foundation buildings theme
resolution: Conflated buildings theme merging OSM, Microsoft, and Google Open Buildings sources; includes a height attribute where a source provides one
license: ODbL (inherited from OSM inclusion; other constituent sources must be ODbL-compatible)
download_route: Anonymous S3/Azure Parquet: s3://overturemaps-us-west-2/release/2026-08-19.0/theme=buildings/type=building/* (or the Azure mirror); typically queried with DuckDB's spatial extension for a bbox filter, no key required.
notes: Global coverage includes India. Since it is a conflation of OSM + Microsoft + Google Open Buildings, for this specific tourist-core bbox it likely reduces to the same OSM data the project already has, plus Microsoft's ML heights where OSM has none -- worth a follow-up query against the bbox to see whether it adds height coverage beyond the project's existing single height-tagged building.
